facts: In 2 N mixed acids, ranging from 2 N HN03 to 2 N H2SO4, the behavior of type 304 reflects its immunity to nitric acid and susceptibility to sulfuric acid.

Stainless steels were reported resistant to fuming nitric acid, but that resistance decreased with increasing temperature up to 160°F; the rate of erosive-corrosive attack decreased with increased rate of flow, probably because of removal of decomposition products from the metal surface.

For sulfuric acid, Kiefer and Renshaw reported that molybdenum-bearing types 316 and 317 were the most resistant at low temperatures, but at about 150°F all of the stainless steels corrode in practically all concentrations of acid up to 95 percent.
Roach and Hall reported that molybdenum-bearing stainless steels were useful, at room temperature, in concentrations of sulfuric acid below 15 percent and above 85 percent.
